question: 'Ganga Dussehra' is celebrated in the month of _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**June**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ganga Dussehra**, also known as **Gangavataran**, is a major **Hindu festival** celebrated to commemorate the descent of the holy **River Ganga** from heaven to earth.
 
• The festival is observed on the **Dashami** (10th day) of the **Shukla Paksha** (waxing phase of the moon) during the **Hindu month** of **Jyeshtha**.
 
• In the **Gregorian calendar**, this auspicious day typically falls in the month of **June**, though occasionally it may begin in late **May** depending on the lunar cycle.
 
• The festival marks the successful culmination of the intense penance performed by **King Bhagiratha**, who sought to bring the river to earth to liberate the souls of his ancestors. ***Hence, the statement regarding the month is correct.***
 
• It is believed that on this specific day, the goddess **Ganga** descended from the heavens, making it one of the most sacred days for purification and spiritual merit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of the Name**: The word **Dussehra** is derived from the **Sanskrit** words **'Dasha'** (ten) and **'Hara'** (to destroy/remove). It signifies the removal of **ten types of sins** (three physical, four verbal, and three mental) through the grace of the river.
 
• **Prominent Locations**: The festival is celebrated with immense fervor at the **Ghats** of the **Ganga** in holy cities such as **Varanasi**, **Haridwar**, **Rishikesh**, **Prayagraj**, and **Garhmukteshwar**. Devotees gather in **thousands** to take a ritualistic **holy dip** in the waters.
 
• **The Role of Lord Shiva**: According to ancient **Puranas**, the force of the falling **Ganga** was so powerful that it could have swept the earth away. To prevent this, **Lord Shiva** caught the river in his **matted locks** (Jata), releasing her in gentle streams.
 
• **Rituals and Traditions**: On this day, pilgrims perform the **Ganga Aarti** at dusk, offering earthen lamps (**diyas**) and flowers to the river. Many devotees also observe **fasts** and engage in charitable activities (**Daana**) to earn spiritual merit.
 
• **Difference from Ganga Jayanti**: It is important to distinguish this festival from **Ganga Jayanti** (or Ganga Saptami), which is celebrated in the month of **Vaisakha** (April/May) and marks the day the river was reborn after being consumed by **Sage Jahnu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Duration**: While the main festival is on the **tenth day**, the celebrations often span **ten days** leading up to the **Dashami**, involving continuous prayers and religious discourses.
 
• **Cultural Impact**: In states like **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, and **West Bengal**, the festival is a vital part of the cultural fabric, promoting the ecological and spiritual preservation of the **National River** of **India**.
 
• **Environmental Awareness**: In recent years, the government and local bodies use the occasion of **Ganga Dussehra** to promote the **Namami Gange** project and other initiatives aimed at cleaning and rejuvenating the river ecosystem.
